raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father grew wheat and maize, I grow wheat and maize, and that's what I know. The soil here on the North China Plain is suited to it. The government buys it at a set price, so I don't have to worry about finding a market. At my age, I'm not going to start growing something unfamiliar.

My son works in the city. He helps during harvest if he can, but mostly it's me. I have 6 mu of flat land. Same plot every year — wheat goes in after the maize, maize goes in after the wheat. That rotation keeps the land working both seasons.

For wheat, I put in an improved variety — I've been using Jimai 22 for years, it does well here, good resistance to rust. I'll apply compound fertilizer at sowing and then top-dress with urea at jointing. My neighbor says I use too much nitrogen but I'd rather the crop not go hungry. Wheat needs water at winter freeze, jointing, and heading — so four irrigations total including at sowing. I'll spray for aphids and powdery mildew when I see them, maybe twice.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the county supply station. Zhengdan 958 or whatever they have that's similar. I use the rotary tiller to work in the wheat stubble, then seed. Summer rains usually help, but I'll irrigate once if July is dry. Maize doesn't need as many sprays — maybe once for corn borer.

I don't do no-till. I've tried it and I don't trust it. Rotary tillage every time.
